import { Button, Buttons, Form, FormControl, Input, Select, SelectItem, Stack, TextArea, TextContent } from "@/components/ui";

export default function Screen() {
  return (
    <Stack direction="column" gap="l">
      <TextContent size="large-heavy">Contact Us</TextContent>
      <Form name="contact" buttons={<Buttons direction="row"><Button action="submit:contact" variant="primary">Submit</Button><Button action="action:cancel_contact" variant="secondary">Cancel</Button></Buttons>}>
        <FormControl label="Name">
          <Input placeholder="Your full name" type="text" rules={["required", "minLength:2"]}>name</Input>
        </FormControl>
        <FormControl label="Email">
          <Input placeholder="you@example.com" type="email" rules={["required", "email"]}>email</Input>
        </FormControl>
        <FormControl label="Phone">
          <Input placeholder="e.g., +1 555 123 4567" type="text" rules={["required", "minLength:7", "maxLength:20"]}>phone</Input>
        </FormControl>
        <FormControl label="Subject">
          <Select name="subject" placeholder="Select a subject..." rules={["required"]}>
            <SelectItem label="General inquiry">general</SelectItem>
            <SelectItem label="Support">support</SelectItem>
            <SelectItem label="Sales">sales</SelectItem>
            <SelectItem label="Billing">billing</SelectItem>
            <SelectItem label="Feedback">feedback</SelectItem>
          </Select>
        </FormControl>
        <FormControl label="Message">
          <TextArea placeholder="How can we help?" rows={6} rules={["required", "minLength:10"]}>message</TextArea>
        </FormControl>
      </Form>
    </Stack>
  );
}

import { Button, Buttons, Card, CardHeader, Form, FormControl, Input, Stack, SwitchGroup, SwitchItem, TabItem, Tabs, TextCallout, TextContent } from "@/components/ui";

export default function Screen() {
  return (
    <Stack direction="column" gap="l">
      <TextContent size="large-heavy">User Settings</TextContent>
      <Tabs>
        <TabItem value="profile" trigger="Profile">
          <Card variant="card">
            <CardHeader subtitle="Update your personal information and avatar.">Profile</CardHeader>
            <Form name="profile_update" buttons={<Buttons><Button action="submit:profile_update" variant="primary">Save changes</Button><Button action="action:reset_profile_form" variant="secondary">Reset</Button></Buttons>}>
              <FormControl label="Display name">
                <Input placeholder="e.g., Alex Johnson" type="text" rules={["required", "minLength:2", "maxLength:60"]}>display_name</Input>
              </FormControl>
              <FormControl label="Avatar URL">
                <Input placeholder="https://example.com/avatar.png" type="url" rules={["url"]}>avatar_url</Input>
              </FormControl>
            </Form>
          </Card>
        </TabItem>
        <TabItem value="security" trigger="Security">
          <Card variant="card">
            <CardHeader subtitle="Manage sign-in protection and account security.">Security</CardHeader>
            <SwitchGroup variant="sunk">
              <SwitchItem description="Require a verification code when signing in." name="two_fa" value="enabled" checked={false} defaultChecked={true} disabled={false}>Two-factor authentication (2FA)</SwitchItem>
            </SwitchGroup>
            <TextCallout title="Tip" description="After enabling 2FA, you may be asked to set up an authenticator app or backup codes.">info</TextCallout>
          </Card>
        </TabItem>
        <TabItem value="notifications" trigger="Notifications">
          <Card variant="card">
            <CardHeader subtitle="Choose what you want to be notified about.">Notifications</CardHeader>
            <SwitchGroup variant="sunk">
              <SwitchItem description="Receive updates and account messages by email." name="notif_email" value="enabled" checked={true} defaultChecked={true} disabled={false}>Email notifications</SwitchItem>
              <SwitchItem description="Get notified about new features and improvements." name="notif_product" value="enabled" checked={false} defaultChecked={false} disabled={false}>Product updates</SwitchItem>
              <SwitchItem description="Important alerts about sign-ins and security changes." name="notif_security" value="enabled" checked={true} defaultChecked={true} disabled={false}>Security alerts</SwitchItem>
            </SwitchGroup>
          </Card>
        </TabItem>
      </Tabs>
    </Stack>
  );
}

rows.question: Who defines the components
rows.plain: Who decides which building blocks the AI can use?
rows.why: If only your app decides, the AI can't put anything on screen that your app doesn't know how to draw.

cells.text: The spec's 27 components plus McpMutation, and the app's own components, each declared with its props
cells.plain: A fixed set, plus your app's own

cells.text: The app's library (Zod schemas); 53 components in its benchmark library
The catalog named in createSurface: the basic catalog or the app's own
cells.plain: A basic set, or your app's own

cells.text: The app's catalog (Zod schemas), or ready-made ones

rows.question: Markup or scripts from the model
rows.plain: Can the AI send its own code?
rows.why: Code from an AI can do things nobody checked, so it has to be cleaned or locked away first.

cells.text: No. Text is always drawn as text
cells.plain: No: text is always shown as text

cells.text: No HTML; the default library renders Markdown and code blocks
cells.plain: No code; formatted text (Markdown) is allowed

cells.text: No; the basic Text allows simple Markdown without HTML, images or links

cells.plain: Yes: it has to be cleaned first

cells.text: Yes: runs as code, needs a sandbox

rows.question: Styling from the model
rows.plain: Can the AI choose colours and styles?
rows.why: When it can't, every screen keeps your brand's look.

cells.text: No: only the catalog's variants and tones; the app's theme sets the colours
cells.plain: No: it picks from a few named looks

cells.text: Variants and sizes from the library
Variants, plus a theme colour (primaryColor) in createSurface
cells.plain: Named looks, plus a theme colour

rows.question: Pictures
rows.why: A web address written by an AI can point anywhere, including somewhere that tracks your users.

cells.text: Names from the app's registry, or names the app looks up, never URLs

rows.question: Actions that change data
rows.plain: What happens when someone presses a button that changes something?
rows.why: This is where an AI mistake costs money or deletes data.

cells.text: Must be wrapped in McpMutation; the tool must be in the app's registry; params checked against the tool's schema by the parser, the browser and the server
cells.plain: Only actions your app lists, checked three times

cells.text: Mutation("tool", args) run by a button; the prompt lists the tools; checking a call is left to the app's tool provider
cells.plain: Actions by name; checking them is up to your app

cells.text: A button sends an event (name and context) to the agent, which handles it
cells.plain: A message goes to the AI agent, which decides

cells.text: Named actions declared in the catalog; params are free-form
cells.plain: Actions your app names; what they send isn't checked

rows.question: Confirmation before a risky action
rows.plain: Can the app make sure people confirm before paying or deleting?
rows.why: A confirmation the AI could leave out isn't a safeguard.

cells.text: The app marks tools that need confirmation; the renderer asks in its own words, and nothing in the stream can skip, change or imitate it
cells.plain: Yes: your app decides, and the AI can't skip it

cells.text: None in its language spec or prompt that we found
None in its spec that we found; the agent handles the button's event
An action in the spec can carry confirm, written with the screen
cells.plain: Yes, but the AI writes it, so it can leave it out

rows.question: Field checks before sending
rows.plain: Are forms checked before anything is sent?
rows.why: People see and fix a mistake, such as a wrong email address, before it reaches your systems.

cells.text: required, format (email, number, phone, URL) and length limits, checked by every renderer with its own messages before an action runs; the server checks again
cells.plain: Yes: required fields, emails, phone numbers, lengths

cells.text: Form fields take rules such as required, email, min and maxLength
Inputs and buttons take checks (required, email, regex and more); a failing check disables the button
Validation helpers such as check.required() and check.email()

rows.question: Logic in the stream
rows.plain: Can the AI write logic, like "if this, then that"?
rows.why: Logic makes screens smarter, and harder to predict and check.

cells.text: Expressions, ternaries, built-ins such as @Each and @Filter, live Query()
cells.plain: Yes: formulas, loops and data lookups

rows.question: Changing a screen after it arrives
rows.plain: Can a screen change after it appears, like an order moving to "Delivered"?
rows.why: Status pages and dashboards need to stay current, and the data should come from your app.

cells.text: Updates from the app's own code after the stream, checked like new lines; the model never sends them
cells.plain: Yes: from your app, never from the AI

cells.text: Query() reruns a tool on a refresh interval the model writes
cells.plain: Yes: data the AI asks to refresh on a timer

cells.text: The agent can send updateComponents and updateDataModel at any time
cells.plain: Yes: the AI agent sends changes

cells.text: The app's state changes what's shown; new patches change the spec

rows.question: When drawing can start
rows.plain: When can people start seeing the screen?
rows.why: Seeing something straight away feels much faster than waiting for the whole reply.

cells.text: Re-parsed on every chunk; references resolve as they arrive
Once the root component's message has arrived
cells.plain: Once the main part has arrived

rows.question: Native iPhone and Android
rows.plain: Does it draw real iPhone and Android screens?
rows.why: Native screens look and feel like the rest of a phone app.

cells.text: SwiftUI (iPhone, iPad, Mac) and Jetpack Compose (Android), passing the same conformance cases as the web
Web runtimes and email; its README lists mobile, but we found no iOS or Android package in its repository
Flutter, through Google's GenUI SDK; SwiftUI and Jetpack Compose are on its roadmap
React for the web; React Native uses other components

rows.question: Web frameworks
rows.plain: Which kinds of websites can show it?
rows.why: Teams use different tools; one format that works in all of them is easier to adopt.

cells.text: React, and <omni-screen> for Vue, Svelte, Angular or plain HTML
React, Vue, Svelte, Angular, and a no-build browser bundle
React, Vue, Svelte, Solid; also PDF, email and video
cells.plain: Most websites, plus PDFs and email

rows.question: Inside AI chat apps (MCP Apps)
rows.plain: Can it show screens inside Claude or ChatGPT?
rows.why: More and more people use apps from inside an AI chat.

cells.text: @omni-ir/mcp: screens inside Claude, ChatGPT, VS Code, Cursor and other MCP Apps hosts, with actions checked by the app's server
None found; OpenUI Lang can travel inside A2UI
Can travel over MCP as a tool's output; the host must draw A2UI
cells.plain: Only where the chat app draws A2UI

cells.text: @json-render/mcp: MCP Apps for Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and VS Code
MCP Apps shows HTML in a sandboxed frame
cells.plain: Yes: chat apps can show web pages in a safe frame

rows.question: Written spec
rows.why: A rulebook lets anyone build a compatible app, so you're not tied to one company.

cells.text: Yes: grammar, document rules, issue codes, renderer rules
Yes: versioned spec with JSON Schemas

rows.question: Shared tests for other implementations
rows.plain: Are there shared tests every version must pass?
rows.why: Shared tests make sure a screen behaves the same on every platform.

cells.text: 127 language-neutral conformance cases, plus 22 transport and 48 field cases; the web, iPhone and Android versions pass them all
cells.plain: Yes, passed on web, iPhone and Android

story.request: A settings screen with a button that permanently deletes my account.
story.omni:
root = Card([title, profileSection, sep, dangerSection])
title = Heading("Settings", level=1)
profileSection = Stack([profileHeading, displayName, bio, save], direction="column", gap="sm")
profileHeading = Heading("Profile", level=2)
$displayName = ""
displayName = Input($displayName, label="Display name", placeholder="Your name")
$bio = ""
bio = Input($bio, label="Bio", placeholder="A short line about you", lines=3)
save = Button("Save profile", action="saveProfile", variant="primary")
saveProfile = McpMutation(save, tool="profile.update", params={displayName: $displayName, bio: $bio})
sep = Divider()
dangerSection = Stack([dangerHeading, dangerText, deleteAccount, unavailable], direction="column", gap="sm")
dangerHeading = Heading("Delete account", level=2)
dangerText = Text("Permanently deleting your account removes all of your data and can't be undone.", tone="muted")
deleteAccount = Button("Delete my account", variant="danger")
unavailable = Text("Account deletion isn't available here.", tone="muted")
story.openui:
root = Stack([header, settingsTabs, dangerCard])
header = CardHeader("Settings", "Manage your account, notifications, and privacy")
settingsTabs = Tabs([accountTab, notificationsTab, privacyTab])

accountForm = Form("account", [nameField, emailField, languageField], accountBtns)
nameField = FormControl("Display name", Input("displayName", "Your name", "text", ["required", "minLength:2"]))
emailField = FormControl("Email", Input("email", "you@example.com", "email", ["required", "email"]))
languageField = FormControl("Language", Select("language", languageOpts, "Select language"))
languageOpts = [SelectItem("en", "English"), SelectItem("es", "Español"), SelectItem("fr", "Français"), SelectItem("de", "Deutsch")]
accountBtns = Buttons([Button("Save changes", "submit:account", "primary")])
notificationsTab = TabItem("notifications", "Notifications", [notificationsCard])
notificationsCard = Card([notificationSwitches], "clear")
notificationSwitches = SwitchGroup([orderSwitch, promoSwitch, securitySwitch], "clear")
orderSwitch = SwitchItem("Order updates", "Shipping and delivery notifications", "orderUpdates", "on", true)
promoSwitch = SwitchItem("Promotions", "Sales, new arrivals, and offers", "promotions", "on", false)
securitySwitch = SwitchItem("Security alerts", "Sign-ins from new devices", "securityAlerts", "on", true)
privacyTab = TabItem("privacy", "Privacy", [privacyCard])
privacyCard = Card([privacySwitches, exportBtns], "clear")
privacySwitches = SwitchGroup([profileSwitch, analyticsSwitch], "clear")
profileSwitch = SwitchItem("Public profile", "Let others see your reviews and wishlists", "publicProfile", "on", false)
analyticsSwitch = SwitchItem("Usage analytics", "Help improve the app with anonymous data", "analytics", "on", true)
exportBtns = Buttons([Button("Download my data", "action:export_data", "secondary")])
dangerCard = Card([dangerHeader, dangerCallout, deleteForm], "sunk")
dangerHeader = CardHeader("Danger zone")
dangerCallout = Callout("error", "Delete account permanently", "This removes your profile, order history, saved addresses, and payment methods. This action cannot be undone.")
deleteForm = Form("deleteAccount", [confirmTextField, confirmCheckField], deleteBtns)
confirmTextField = FormControl("Type DELETE to confirm", Input("confirmText", "DELETE", "text", ["required", "pattern:^DELETE$"]))
confirmCheckField = FormControl("Acknowledgement", CheckBoxGroup("acknowledge", ackOpts, ["required"]))
ackOpts = [CheckBoxItem("I understand this is permanent", "My account and all its data will be erased and cannot be recovered", "understood", false)]
deleteBtns = Buttons([Button("Permanently delete my account", "submit:deleteAccount", "primary", "destructive", "medium")])
